commands.0: BEGIN: task ID, shift 0..47, layer 1..12; only idle
commands.1: X: flattened m*64+k index in ascending order; signed16 sign-extended to48
commands.2: OPEN: next logical tile index; hardware selects a free physical slot
commands.3: W: index k*16+local_n from0 through1023; signed16 sign-extended to48
commands.5: COMMIT: loaded slot becomes READY; this does not release the active slot
commands.6: START: exactly once after COMMIT tile0 and before future OPEN
commands.other: unsupported hardware command; accepted ordered events retire to a fault

capacity_and_progress: The public ingress is one ordered event entry. in_valid&&in_ready accepts an event; command/RAM retirement occurs later. These are separate observations.
Before START, a future OPEN is rejected even if slot1 is free. Sending future OPEN before START is not a preload strategy.
After START, legal next OPEN reserves FREE slot0 or slot1. Loading can overlap computation from the other physically separate SP bank set.
When both slots are occupied, a legal next OPEN can be accepted into the single ingress entry and deferred. Its pending status must not prevent software from draining Y.
The adapter should expose nonblocking event capacity/pending status. A CPU must not wait inside a blocking MMIO transaction for a W slot while it is the only possible Y consumer.
W feed and Y drain need bounded fair service. Polling pending completion alone can deadlock a full-slot OPEN; interleave result capture/writeback/POP while that event remains pending.
slot_lifetime: FREE -> LOADING on OPEN retirement -> READY on COMMIT retirement -> ACTIVE when the scheduler selects the exact next logical tile.
Bias references finish before output publication. The ACTIVE owner remains reserved through all row blocks and the final Y handshake of that logical tile.
On tile-final Y fire the old ACTIVE slot becomes FREE. WAIT_TILE activates the next READY slot, including the directed case where next COMMIT retired on that same old-final-Y clock.
A COMMIT/old-final-Y same-clock event has actual directed hits in both L1 and L2: COMMIT_LAST_Y 27 1 0 143, once per case.
result_and_completion: Hold/capture Y data, task, index, overflow, saturated and last together. POP must acknowledge only the captured result after its actual writeback response, according to the adapter contract.
The core output order is tiled; y_index=m*N+n is the shared-memory address index. output_writes is a count and must not substitute for y_index.
Global final Y publication closes core ingress even under output backpressure. An earlier accepted illegal event still retires and faults before success.
A BEGIN held at the global-final boundary is accepted only after the done pulse clears and belongs to the next task.
Core done alone is insufficient for SoC system_done. Wait for every shared-memory write response, including the final result, and reject a premature successful CPU end.
limitations: This is the core author's integration handoff, not independent RTL acceptance.
W2 CPU integration is not claimed by these core runs.
Official process timing/area/energy and official600 input acceptance remain external.
